pr_title: FIX: iOS Simulator not rendering due to missing CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES
pr_body:
This PR closes #11978

# Objective

Fix rendering on iOS Simulators.

iOS Simulator doesn't support the capability CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES, since 0.13 this started to make iOS Simulator not render anything with the following message being outputted:

```
2024-02-19T14:59:34.896266Z ERROR bevy_render::render_resource::pipeline_cache: failed to create shader module: Validation Error

Caused by:
    In Device::create_shader_module
    
Shader validation error: 


    Type [40] '' is invalid
    Capability Capabilities(CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES) is required
```

## Solution

- Split up NO_ARRAY_TEXTURES_SUPPORT into both NO_ARRAY_TEXTURES_SUPPORT and NO_CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES_SUPPORT and correctly apply NO_ARRAY_TEXTURES_SUPPORT for iOS Simulator using the cfg flag introduced in #10178.

---

## Changelog

### Fixed
- Rendering on iOS Simulator due to missing CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES support.

issue_context.title: iOS Simulator not rendering due to missing CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES capability
issue_context.body:
Seems like the iOS Simulator uses an MTLFeatureSet not including CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES so currently nothing gets rendered with this error message:

```
2024-02-19T14:59:34.896266Z ERROR bevy_render::render_resource::pipeline_cache: failed to create shader module: Validation Error

Caused by:
    In Device::create_shader_module
    
Shader validation error: 


    Type [40] '' is invalid
    Capability Capabilities(CUBE_ARRAY_TEXTURES) is required
```

Saw that this was discussed in #10266 and that it might lead to a potential issue. Any pointers on how this could be fixed?

I'm open to work on it and make a PR for it, simply just using the DownLevel flags don't seem to work as it will just lead to a downstream error in naga_oil instead.

## Bevy version

0.13

## Relevant system information

XCode 15.2.0 - iOS 17.2 Simulator - iPhone 15 Pro

```ignore
`AdapterInfo { name: "Apple iOS simulator GPU", vendor: 0, device: 0, device_type: DiscreteGpu, driver: "", driver_info: "", backend: Metal }`
```

review_comments: A comment on why this is necessary should be added here in case this changes in the future.
Yeah, hopefully Apple eventually adds support for this, so good idea to add a comment. Fixed!
